items.name: Council of Europe Framework Convention on AI (CETS No. 225)
items.summary: The first legally binding international AI treaty, covering human rights, democracy and the rule of law. The EU ratified on 15 May 2026. Entry-into-force status and the full ratification count were not confirmed.
items.citizen: A treaty that commits signing countries to protect your rights when governments or companies use AI.
items.note: Check the treaty office page for current ratification count.

items.name: UN General Assembly Resolution A/RES/79/325
items.summary: Created the Independent International Scientific Panel on AI and the Global Dialogue on AI Governance.
items.citizen: The UN's decision to set up a global expert panel and a yearly forum on AI.

items.name: Independent International Scientific Panel on AI
items.summary: First in-person meeting in Madrid in April 2026; preliminary report released 1 July 2026. Membership details were not confirmed.
items.citizen: A UN panel of scientists that reports on what AI can do and what risks it poses.
items.note: Verify dates and membership on un.org.

items.name: UN Global Dialogue on AI Governance
items.status: First session 6–7 July 2026, Geneva; next 3–4 May 2027, New York
items.summary: Produced a Co-Chairs' Summary across four themes: opportunities, bridging divides, safe and trustworthy AI, and human rights and accountability. No adopted decisions.
items.citizen: A global meeting where governments discuss AI rules. It can talk and recommend, not enforce.

items.name: New Delhi Declaration on AI Impact
items.summary: Focuses on shared benefits, sovereignty, energy-efficient infrastructure and inclusion. Critics note no enforceable safety standards and little civil-society representation. Whether the US and China signed was not confirmed.
items.citizen: A promise by many countries to make AI work for everyone, with no way to force them to keep it.

items.name: OECD Due Diligence Guidance for Responsible AI
items.summary: Voluntary guidance on due diligence for AI. The OECD AI Principles themselves are not covered by the sources used here.
items.citizen: Advice to companies on checking their AI for harm. Not law.
items.note: Verify on oecd.org; add the OECD AI Principles.

items.name: APEC AI Initiative
items.citizen: Asia-Pacific governments agreeing to cooperate on AI.

gaps: Not yet covered: OECD AI Principles, G7 Hiroshima Process, UNESCO Recommendation on AI Ethics, ISO/IEC 42001, Bletchley/Seoul/Paris summit statements.
